name: Seychelles
summary: Children are reserved heirs under the Civil Code (art. 913): reportedly one half with one child, two thirds with two, three quarters with three or more. The Constitutional Court upheld this in 2013. Seychelles has a Trusts Act 2021 and Foundations Act 2009 that offer anti-forced-heirship protection.
reserved_share: Children: reportedly 1/2 with one child, 2/3 with two, 3/4 with three or more (art. 913 Civil Code; secondary source). Upheld as proportionate by the Constitutional Court in Durup v Brassel (2013), endorsed by the Court of Appeal (2014).
foreign_law_note: Forced heirship applies to citizens and, reportedly, to foreigners owning property in Seychelles under its civil law. Foreign-law choice for movables not confirmed.
trust_note: Trusts Act 2021 (Act 34 of 2021, in force 6 Aug 2021, replacing the International Trusts Act 1994) covers Seychelles trusts and foreign trusts (Part IV, s. 81); commentary says foreign forced-heirship claims are not recognised, and no estate duty applies to international trust assets. Foundations Act 2009 has an anti-forced-heirship section (unofficial consolidation; verify). Domestic law still applies to a Seychellois's own estate.
open_questions: Fractions come from a commercial guide; verify against the Civil Code.
Text of Trusts Act 2021 forced-heirship provision not read; official page blocked.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
